item.title: Gambonanza Endgame Tips - Closing Out Runs Without Throwing Them
item.description: Winning the opening is not the hard part of Gambonanza. The hard part is the last few pieces, when the board is small, the Crumble counter is running, the Stalemate Counter is creeping toward its limit, and one wrong capture hands the game back. I have lost more runs in the final three pieces than in every boss fight combined. This guide is everything I do at the end of a match to actually finish it.

item.title: Gambonanza Money & Shop Guide - How to Earn, Save, and Spend Gold
item.description:
The Economy, Without the Noise

THE SHORT VERSION

Gold comes from winning games, Gold Tiles, and specific Gambits. There are no investment tables, no compound interest, and no hidden catch-up mechanic. A healthy run is one where you can afford one good buy per shop and still have a buffer for a bad boss fight.

Where Your Money Comes From

Source How it works
Winning a game The main source. You earn gold for capturing every enemy piece
Gold Tiles Landing a piece on a Gold Tile pays out
Gold Gambits A few Gambits convert captures or landings into gold
Selling a Gambit You can sell a Gambit you no longer use to recover part of its cost
Pro tip:
The real economy rule
You cannot farm gold forever. Crumble and the Stalemate Counter keep games moving, so every turn spent stalling is a turn you could be capturing and earning. Economy and tempo are the same skill in this game.

How the Shop Works

Every shop offers a fixed layout. Read it before you spend.

item.title: Gambonanza Controller & Gamepad Guide: Strains, Gambit Collection & Deck Navigation
item.description:
EARLY GAME
Gambonanza has full controller support, and the 1.5.3 hotfix fixed the two menu flows that were roughest on a gamepad: the Strains menu and the Gambit collection tab. If you play on Steam Deck or with a controller, these fixes are the difference between a smooth run and a fight with the UI. The control scheme itself is simple once you know where everything lives.
A smooth Strains menu is only useful if you open it. Read your modifiers once per run and adjust your build before the first turn, because the menu lists exactly what higher tiers change.

Why Controller Support Matters Here

Gambonanza is a menu-heavy game. A run involves the board, the Gambit sidebar, the Shop, the Graveyard, the Strains menu, and the Gambit collection. Each is a distinct interface. When controller navigation works, the game feels native on a handheld. When it does not, you feel every menu.

item.title: Gambonanza on Steam Deck: Best Settings for Text, Cursor & Controller
item.description:
MID GAME
Gambonanza is officially Steam Deck Verified as of v1.5.0, and the 1.5.x line fixed the two things that hurt handheld play most: text readability and an invisible-cursor bug on some Linux setups. Set aside two minutes before your first run. Turn on the readability improvements, confirm there is no letterboxing, and use the updated Strains menu navigation. That is the whole checklist.
Do not start a serious climb on default settings. Confirm full-screen display, turn on skip animations, and test the Strains menu before your first real game on the Deck.

Why the Deck Needs Its Own Setup Guide

Gambonanza is a busy game. A small chess board, a dense Gambit sidebar, and a compact HUD are all fighting for space. On desktop you have monitor real estate to spare. On the Steam Deck you have a seven-inch screen and a controller. That is exactly why the 1.5.0 UI revamp targeted the Deck, and why Verified status matters: Valve’s criteria include legibility, default input, and stability on the handheld.

item.title: Gambonanza UI & Text Readability After 1.5: Read the Board Faster
item.description:
MID GAME
The v1.5.0 UI revamp makes text easier to read, with the biggest impact on Steam Deck. Combined with the algebraic notation toggle and the 1.5.3 hover-info fix, the board and its tooltips are now legible on small screens. Readability is not cosmetic in a game this dense. Clearer text means faster decisions and fewer mistakes.
Use the clearer text to identify the board state first, then check the Gambits that apply. Readability is a workflow: scan the board, then the sidebar, in that order.

Why Readability Is a Real Advantage

Gambonanza throws a lot at you at once. A small board, a Gambit sidebar, a Shop, and a HUD all compete for attention. Every time you have to squint or re-read a tooltip, you lose tempo. In a turn-based roguelike, tempo is everything: the player who reads the board faster makes more moves in the same amount of thinking time, and makes fewer misreads.

item.title: Gambonanza Tips & Tricks-25 Pro Tips That Changed How I Play
item.description:
25 Tips That Changed How I Play Gambonanza

I’ve logged 100+ hours in Gambonanza and these are the tips I wish I knew on day one. Not obvious stuff like “read the tutorial”-these are the insights that separate players who consistently win from players who rage-quit after boss 3.

The Single Most Important Tip

Enter every boss fight with enough gold for a comfortable shop pass. You cannot retry a lost run, so the gold you save before a boss is the gold you spend on the next one. This one habit alone will win you runs. Everything else on this page is secondary.
